state.task: The user has accepted inline translated source text with explicit language keys, e.g. title="Tasks"@{nl="Taken",de="Aufgaben"}, and asks to update every draft plus outdated docs. Do not reopen that direction. Adoption, token efficiency, readable # descriptions, one canonical mechanism, no boilerplate, faithful business logic and real sharing remain requirements. Consult on unresolved label placement and ownership semantics before implementation. Current syntax parser cannot type-check or execute apps.
state.evidence: A scoped inventory resolves all 1892 label targets: 913 fields, 374 enum cases, 164 models, 145 scenario parameters, 144 scenarios, 67 roles, 35 contracts, 24 packages, 22 derived fields, 2 bool cases and 2 generated CRUD actions. There are 1521 label rows; 256 grouped rows avoid copying 371 translations. Among 724 named messages, 699 have one use and 25 have two; every one of 373 description messages is static and used once. All 51 existing owner tables contain en,nl and no absent variants. One typed ICU plural message is reused; two exported words cross owners. There are 48 description-only message import lines; one separate message-only import shares add and field_title across owners. Existing enum field-type reuse carries value labels, and standard exact identifier/type captions and runtime wording are implicit.
state.representation: Implement one source string plus @{locale=STRING-or-null,...} descriptor value. Keys can be NAME for simple tags or quoted STRING for regional tags, e.g. @{"pt-BR"="Tarefas"}; no general object/data localization. A quoted source string without a suffix stays ordinary literal text. Empty @{} explicitly creates a source-only message descriptor. Descriptions retain raw # prose and allow one suffix on their final prose line; variants translate the complete joined description. A backslash directly before @{ quotes that marker, with only that one backslash removed; other raw prose backslashes remain literal. Reused static descriptions may use existing #= paths. Message assets derive from canonical owner/slot, not source offsets, public operation names or user-authored keys.
state.source_scope: Each logical app or package pins the authored source language to en unless its declaration header has source="other-tag". Header source applies to its description and owned message values, including a composed app with no Given section. Importing/composing never retags another owner's variants. File moves do not change ownership or language. The existing context locale default controls fallback/viewer preference only and never source language. Resolve/canonicalize BCP47 tags, reject duplicate variants including the owner source tag, and report missing coverage. No source override is needed in the current English corpus.
state.shared_and_typed: Replace mandatory messages locale-column containers with Given leaf declarations: [export] message name[(typed_parameters)] = the same inline message value. Keep names only for actual sharing, including the 25 reused names and assets replacing current grouped bindings. All single-use descriptions/UI text become inline and their unused keys/imports disappear. Named ICU declarations keep explicit signatures. Anonymous parameterized inline descriptors use existing postfix call with named arguments, whose types are resolved from expressions; every placeholder across variants must bind explicitly and validate, with no implicit capture. Common defaults/inherited schema assets stay implicit. Stored data, fixtures, machine names, guards, effects, policies, queries and existing BDD observations retain meaning. There is no message runtime, ICU checker or renderer yet.
state.label_alternatives: The compound-attribute alternative uses one trailing label= attribute for all authored declaration captions. A scalar is a static source string, descriptor or shared message path. On a field/parameter needing enum or bool captions, the same attribute can be a closed object {text=caption,values={case=caption,...}}, omitting text when unchanged. Case keys are stable wire values; inherited case overrides use this same form. A CRUD declaration has a closed label={create=caption,update=caption,delete=caption} for enabled operations only. Model/contract/role/package/scenario/derived-field captions remain scalar. This adds bounded object interpretation but requires no enum grammar change. A separate-attributes alternative has label= for captions and labels={case=...} for field cases plus create_label/update_label/delete_label CRUD slots; it is more explicit by slot but adds names and productions. Adjacent target bindings preserve existing grouped target shape, make case/action targets uniform and localize translations directly; they retain repeated target identities and separate label metadata from the actual declarations. None changes machine identifiers or business access.

labels.instructions: Which single canonical label placement best fits the accepted inline direction, actual field/case/action targets, inherited labels and repetition limits? Weigh each approach's syntax cost, clarity and locality. Choose unresolved if those contracts cannot be justified from the evidence.

criteria.compound: Place one label attribute on the owner, using a scalar for simple captions and a bounded object for caption/case or CRUD slots. Accept context-specific closed object shapes for fewer attribute names and unchanged enum syntax.
criteria.separate: Attach distinct caption, case-label and per-CRUD-action attributes at owners. Accept additional attribute names/productions for direct slot-specific wording and fewer context-dependent object shapes.
criteria.bindings: Keep owner-adjacent target-binding declarations with inline message values and grouped targets. Accept repeated paths and separated metadata for uniform target rules and direct existing-group reuse.
criteria.unresolved: Do not choose because source ownership, inherited overrides or label attachment lacks enough evidence to support one canonical representation.

scope.instructions: Is a pinned en source language with explicit logical-owner source overrides coherent for inline descriptors, including composed-app metadata and imported assets, when it remains separate from deployment default/viewer locale and preserves canonical owner identity under file moves?

typed.instructions: Can anonymous inline ICU descriptors use existing postfix calls with explicit named arguments and inferred argument types, alongside explicitly typed shared message declarations, without implicit lexical capture or changing ordinary string/data semantics, provided the specified placeholder/type/provenance checks are implemented?
